key_insight: Latent-conditioned parameterized quantum circuits (LPQCs) use a classical latent variable to generate quantum circuit parameters, and are proven to universally approximate distributions over quantum states.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical quantum generative modeling route for heterogeneous state ensembles in quantum simulation, chemistry, and machine learning without preparing each state individually.
method: Sample a latent variable from a prior distribution.
Use classical neural networks to map the latent code to quantum circuit parameters.
Generate quantum states with a parameterized quantum circuit; a multimodal prior and mixture-of-experts design help optimization and reduce barren plateaus.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on a synthetic multi-cluster ensemble of mixed quantum states and a QM9-derived ensemble of 3-D molecular structures, with LPQC outperforming recent quantum baselines and remaining competitive with classical baselines at lower output dimensionality.
watch_item: Performance depends on effective latent prior design and circuit training, so optimization stability and scalability may still be challenging on larger, noisier quantum hardware.
paper_title: Latent-Conditioned Parameterized Quantum Circuits as Universal Approximators for Distributions over Quantum States
